subject: Residency handoff: conditional egress, replication proof & next steps
messages:
From: Lena Mueller <lena.mueller@medtech-eu.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Cc: privacy@medtech-eu.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 09:21:00 +0200
Subject: Residency confirmation & replication behaviour question

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Two quick follow-ups from our DPO:

1) For EU-pin customers, can you confirm whether any transient replication or cache warming can result in customer data touching non-EU compute for more than ephemeral key-value operations (e.g., NTP windows, cache prefetch, telemetry pings)? Our legal team needs simple language to put in the DPA addendum.

2) We also need an example of the operational evidence you can provide post-onboarding — something our auditors can see: a sample telemetry path, a signed subprocessor roster, and a diagram showing the failover sequence and time bounds.

If you can attach the sample artifacts or point us to a drive link that would be great. We aim to close the residency checklist by next Friday.

Best,
Lena
Lena Mueller
Head of Privacy
MedTech EU

---
Lena Mueller
MedTech EU
From: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
To: Lena Mueller <lena.mueller@medtech-eu.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 12:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation & replication behaviour question

Hi Lena,

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front:
- For EU-pin customers we guarantee that persistent storage, logs, and model traces remain in-region. Transient KV cache entries used for latency-sensitive inference may be staged outside the EU only for up to 30 seconds during proactive cache-warm operations, and are encrypted in transit with customer-keyed TLS. We will include that exact phrase in the DPA addendum.
- We can provide a short packet of operational evidence: a residency dataflow diagram, the subprocessor roster signed by legal, and sample telemetry traces showing an EU->EU path plus a controlled failover example.

Attaching the diagram and roster for initial review (see attachments). I'll coordinate with Kimberly for the telemetry extract — Marissa will help with the compliance wording for the DPA addendum.

Next steps proposed:
1) Kimberly to produce a redacted sample telemetry path (audit-ready) by Fri 2027-09-03.
2) Marissa to draft the DPA addendum language and circulate for sign-off by Mon 2027-09-06.
3) Jonas to provide the residency diagram and annotated failover timeline (attached).

Is that cadence OK?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: residency-dataflow-diagram.pdf, subprocessor-roster-2027-09.csv
From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, Lena Mueller <lena.mueller@medtech-eu.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 07:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation & replication behaviour question

On Wed, 1 Sep 2027, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com wrote:
> For EU-pin customers we guarantee that persistent storage, logs, and model traces remain in-region. Transient KV cache entries used for latency-sensitive inference may be staged outside the EU only for up to 30 seconds during proactive cache-warm operations...

Lena / team — quick note from ops: the 30s window is conservative and measured on our current fleet under normal network conditions (p99). It covers: proactive prefetches, cross-region control-plane handshakes during model rollout, and a short-lived replication path used when we shift a warm token cache during a vertical scale. We do not ship payloads or model inputs to the remote region outside of that ephemeral context.

Telemetry we'll provide:
- timestamped request/response hops with AS path and region tags (redacted identifiers)
- a sample failover trace where EU primary goes read-only and a regional fallback is invoked (annotated with durations)

I'll upload the redacted telemetry export to the shared drive link Jonas included. Note: the telemetry example will be redacted to strip customer PII and will include cryptographic checksums for trace integrity.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: Lena Mueller <lena.mueller@medtech-eu.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.example.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: DPA addendum language proposal (draft)

Hi Lena,

Thanks for the patience — attaching an initial DPA addendum paragraph for your legal team to review. Summary:
- Residency commitment: persistent customer content, logs, and model artifacts are stored and processed only within the EU region for EU-pin customers.
- Ephemeral processing: short-lived cache/warm-up operations may transiently touch non-EU compute for no longer than 30 seconds; such processing does not include persistent storage, model checkpoints, or unredacted logs. All transient operations occur over TLS and are logged with region tags.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide a signed subprocessor roster, a residency diagram, and a redacted telemetry sample upon onboarding and annually thereafter.

Action items for MedTech EU: please confirm whether the 30-second upper bound is acceptable in principle, and whether you need any additional commitments around KMS key locality or audit frequency.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Lena Mueller <lena.mueller@medtech-eu.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 15:42:00 +0200
Subject: Re: DPA addendum language proposal (draft)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Two items from the DPO review:

1) The 30-second window is acceptable as long as it is surfaced in the addendum and in the onboarding checklist with the exact operational definition (i.e., what counts as "ephemeral processing"). Please include the three operation types Kimberly listed.

2) We would like confirmation that for EU-pin customers MedTech EU can request a KMS key to be bound to EU-only HSMs for encryption-at-rest of customer metadata (not model weights). Is that something Redwood offers as an onboarding option?

If you can get back to us on the KMS question by Monday we'll route the addendum internally and aim to sign next Wed.

Best,
Lena
